You will be asked to approve the first action that reaches outside your workspace — that card is the whole learning curve.

1.answer: No. Model usage is drawn from credits, and every plan includes an allowance: 1,000 credits once on Free, 10,000 a month on Pro, 35,000 on Team. One credit costs $0.001. On a paid plan you can also bring your own model key, billed with no markup. These are launch prices; sign-up is by waitlist for now.

10.answer: An AI agent framework is the runtime and library layer for building, coordinating, and governing autonomous AI agents. It supplies the loop, the tool calls, memory, and coordination, and leaves security, cost control, and operations to you. OpenLegion ships those as the product rather than the exercise: policy-checked tool calls, per-agent budgets, a credential vault, approvals, and receipts.
10.question: What is an AI agent framework?

11.answer: A framework is a library you build with; a hosted platform is a product you sign in to. With a framework you own the runtime, the secrets, the scaling, and the bill. OpenLegion is the second kind: agents are rows in a managed database, each task runs on demand, and the security and cost controls are enforced for you rather than assembled by you.
11.question: What is an AI agent framework vs managed hosting?

12.answer: Work is organised as goals and tasks. Your assistant creates the agents a goal needs and delegates tasks to them, each with a deadline; a delegated task can spawn short-lived helpers and hands its result back for review. Agents never block on each other — every hand-off is an event with a correlation id and a deadline that escalates if it passes. You see all of it as threads, one per agent.
12.question: How does agent coordination work in OpenLegion?

13.answer: It means treating the agent as something that can be talked into a mistake. The controls that matter are the ones that hold when the model is wrong: secrets the model never sees, a policy engine in front of every tool call, a sandbox with no egress by default, untrusted content that cannot trigger an irreversible action on its own, and a human approval for anything that reaches a third party or destroys data.
13.question: What does AI agent security mean for autonomous agents?

2.answer: Research and summarising, drafting and rewriting, watching a channel and replying, keeping a schedule, running code in a sandbox, and producing a deliverable you can share with a link. Agents work in the web app on every plan, add Telegram and webhooks on Pro, and add Slack and inbound email on Team; on every plan they can read your Google Calendar and the Drive files you pick. What they do not do yet: browse the web signed in as you, make phone calls, or send email on your behalf.
2.question: What kinds of tasks can OpenLegion agents actually automate?

3.answer: OpenLegion is a hosted platform for AI agent teams. You describe the work in one sentence; an assistant creates the teammates it needs and delegates to them. Each agent is a durable record that runs when there is something to do, so an idle agent costs nothing. Every tool call is checked by one policy engine and leaves a receipt, and anything that reaches a third party, deletes data, or acts on untrusted content stops for your approval.
3.question: What is OpenLegion?

4.answer: Frameworks give you the parts; OpenLegion is the running product. You do not assemble a runtime, a queue, a vault, and a dashboard — you sign in and describe the job. Where a framework leaves permissions and cost to you, OpenLegion enforces them: every tool call is an intent through one policy engine, every agent has a budget, secrets stay in a vault the model never sees, and irreversible actions wait for a human.
4.question: How is OpenLegion different from CrewAI or other agent frameworks?

5.answer: You choose a preset, not a model id: Smartest for work you would hand to your best person, Smart for everyday reasoning, Normal for fast, cheap chores. Presets map to current frontier models, reached through one gateway, and are re-checked as new models ship. You can set a preset per agent or a default for the workspace. On a paid plan you can bring your own model key instead, billed with no markup. Traffic on our platform keys is zero-retention and opted out of training.
5.question: What LLM providers does OpenLegion support?

6.answer: Credentials live in a vault and are injected outside the model: the agent holds a handle, never a key. Every tool call is an intent that the policy engine checks before anything executes, and the result is recorded as a receipt you can read. A compromised prompt cannot read a secret that was never in its context.
6.question: How does OpenLegion handle API key security?

7.answer: No. OpenLegion is a hosted web app — sign in with Google and you are running. There is no server to provision, no Docker, and no infrastructure of your own to keep alive. Agents are records in our database and each task runs on demand, so a workspace with a hundred agents costs the same at rest as one with none.
7.question: Do I need Kubernetes or cloud infrastructure to run OpenLegion?

8.answer: Yes — that is what it is for. Tenant isolation is row-level security on every table, verified by a cross-tenant test suite in CI. Every tool call is policy-checked and receipted, agents run under per-agent budgets, and irreversible actions stop for a human. The workspace owner can export everything on every plan; on Team and Enterprise the export also includes the activity log.
8.question: Can I run OpenLegion in production?

9.answer: Not today. OpenLegion v2 is a hosted platform, and self-hosting is not something you can buy. The previous-generation engine is still published under the PolyForm Perimeter License 1.0.1 and can be run on your own machine, but it is a different product. If on-premises is a hard requirement, it is an Enterprise conversation.

section1.p1: This Privacy Policy describes how OpenLegion ("we," "us," "our") collects, uses, and discloses information when you visit openlegion.ai (the "Website") or use our hosted AI agent platform, APIs, and related services (collectively, the "Service").
section1.p2: By using the Service, you consent to the practices described in this Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the Service.
section1.title: 1. Introduction

section10.text: If you are a California resident, you have additional rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), including the right to know what personal information we collect, request deletion, and opt out of the sale of personal information. We do not sell personal information. To exercise your CCPA rights, contact support@openlegion.ai.
section10.title: 10. California Residents (CCPA)

section11.p1: If you are in the EEA, our legal basis for processing your personal data includes: (a) your consent; (b) performance of a contract; (c) compliance with a legal obligation; and (d) our legitimate interests (improving and securing the Service) where those interests are not overridden by your data protection rights.
section11.p2: You may lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority if you believe we have violated your rights under the GDPR.
section11.title: 11. European Economic Area (GDPR)

section12.text: Your information may be transferred to and processed in the United States or other countries where our service providers operate. These countries may have different data protection laws than your jurisdiction. By using the Service, you consent to such transfers.
section12.title: 12. International Data Transfers

section13.text: The Service is not directed to individuals under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we become aware that we have collected data from a child, we will delete it promptly.
section13.title: 13. Children's Privacy

section14.text: We may update this Privacy Policy at any time. Changes will be reflected by updating the "Last updated" date at the top of this page. Your continued use of the Service after any changes constitutes acceptance of the updated Privacy Policy.
section14.title: 14. Changes to This Policy

section15.text: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or wish to exercise your rights, contact us at:
section15.title: 15. Contact Us

items.0: Account information: the name and email address your Google account provides when you sign in. We do not store a password for you.
items.1: Payment information: billing details processed by our third-party payment processor (Stripe). We do not store card numbers on our servers.
items.2: Communications: information you provide when contacting us by email, live chat (Tawk.to), or Discord.
items.3: Customer Data: the messages you send your agents, the agents and tasks you create, files you upload or connect, and the memory your agents write.

items.0: Usage data: Pages visited, features used, timestamps, referral URLs, and general interaction patterns.
items.1: Device information: Browser type, operating system, screen resolution, and device identifiers.
items.2: IP address: Collected for security, analytics, and approximate geolocation purposes.
items.3: Cookies and similar technologies: See Section 6 below.

section3.intro: We use the information we collect to:

items.0: Provide, operate, and maintain the Service;
items.1: Process payments and send billing-related communications;
items.2: Respond to your inquiries and provide customer support;
items.3: Analyze usage patterns to improve the Service (via Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity);
items.4: Detect, prevent, and address technical issues, fraud, or abuse;
items.5: Send transactional emails (account confirmation, password reset, billing receipts);

section3.noSell: We do not sell your personal information. We do not use Customer Data to train AI models, and model traffic sent on our platform keys is zero-retention and opted out of training at the provider.
section3.title: 3. How We Use Your Information

section4.intro: We use the following third-party services that may collect information as described in their respective privacy policies:

items.0: Google Analytics — website analytics and traffic measurement.
items.1: Microsoft Clarity — session recording and heatmaps for UX analysis.
items.2: Tawk.to — live chat widget for customer support.
items.3: Stripe — payment processing and subscription billing.
items.4: Model providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), reached through our model gateway — AI inference. Traffic sent on our platform keys is zero-retention and opted out of training; prompts and agent data are otherwise governed by those providers' terms.

section4.review: We encourage you to review the privacy policies of these third-party services.
section4.title: 4. Third-Party Services

section5.intro: We may share your information only in the following circumstances:

items.0: Service providers: Third-party vendors who assist in operating the Service (hosting, payment processing, analytics) under contractual obligations to protect your data.
items.1: Legal requirements: When required by law, subpoena, court order, or governmental request.
items.2: Protection of rights: To enforce our Terms of Service, protect our rights or safety, or investigate fraud.
items.3: Business transfers: In connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction.

section5.title: 5. Data Sharing & Disclosure

section6.control: You can control cookies through your browser settings. Disabling cookies may affect the functionality of the Service.
section6.intro: We use cookies and similar technologies (pixels, local storage) for analytics, functionality, and security purposes. The Website uses:

section6.title: 6. Cookies & Tracking Technologies

You can export your workspace or erase it at any time from Settings; erasing removes your workspace's records and the files stored with them. Backups expire on their own rolling schedule, and we retain billing records for as long as the law requires.
section7.title: 7. Data Retention

section8.text: We implement commercially reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your information. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or electronic storage is 100% secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security and are not liable for any unauthorized access, data breach, or loss of data.
section8.title: 8. Data Security

section9.contact: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at support@openlegion.ai. We will respond within 30 days (or as required by applicable law).
section9.intro: Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have the following rights regarding your personal information:

items.0: Access: Request a copy of the personal information we hold about you.
items.1: Correction: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.
items.2: Deletion: Request deletion of your personal information, subject to legal retention requirements.
items.3: Portability: Request your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
items.4: Objection: Object to processing of your personal information for certain purposes.
items.5: Opt-out of sale: We do not sell personal information. If this changes, we will provide a clear opt-out mechanism.

architecture.title: Agents are records. Work runs on demand, then stops.
architecture.summary: An agent is a row in a database, not a server: creating one is instant, and an idle one costs nothing but storage. When a message, a schedule, or another agent gives it work, a single run starts under a lease, goes through one policy engine for every tool call, writes its receipts, and ends. Anything that arrived from outside carries an untrusted label the whole way through.

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.heading: What we can promise, and
securityPage.lede: OpenLegion runs agents that read your data and act on your behalf. Below is what the product actually enforces today, written plainly enough that you can hold us to it — and, at the end, the things we are not claiming.
securityPage.guaranteesHeading: Eight things that are true today
securityPage.approvals: Three walls, and only three, so that a card still means something when one appears: reaching a third party on your behalf, deleting data, and acting on content that arrived from outside your workspace. Everything else runs and leaves a receipt you can read afterwards. Decisions are made in the app, by a workspace owner or admin — never by an agent, and never by us; your channels can tell you a card is waiting.
securityPage.notClaimed: We hold no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA certification, and we don't describe the product as "GDPR compliant" or "EU AI Act compliant" — compliance is a property of how you use a system, not a badge a vendor awards itself. No system that reads the open web is immune to prompt injection; we publish no attack-success percentages, because a number without a published method is marketing. Web search and page fetches run on our servers, not inside the code sandbox, so "fully sandboxed" would be wrong. We have not commissioned a third-party penetration test. When any of that changes, this page changes with it.
securityPage.data: You can erase your workspace from Settings at any time; erasing removes your workspace's rows and the files stored with them. The workspace owner can export its data on every plan, and on Team and above the export includes the activity log. Conversation history is kept until you delete it or erase the workspace. We do not sell personal information and we do not train models on your data.
securityPage.contact: Found something we should know about? Email {email} and we will answer.

features.title: Security the agent can't talk its way past
features.lede: The model is never the final authority. Each control below is enforced by the platform, outside the model, the same way for every customer you serve.

items.title: Every action is checked, then receipted
items.body: Each tool call is an intent that passes one policy engine before it runs. Afterwards there is a receipt: who asked, what ran and what it cost.

items.title: Approval at three walls, and only three
items.body: Reaching a third party, deleting data and acting on untrusted content. Your customer approves in your UI and the decision is recorded as theirs. Everything else runs, so an approval still means something.

items.title: A cap for each customer, matching your plans
items.body: Monthly and daily credit caps, hard or soft, renewing on your customer's billing day. A reached cap refuses the run before it starts and sends a webhook you can turn into an upgrade screen.

items.title: Keys the model never sees
items.body: Credentials live in a vault. The model holds a handle, the broker injects the secret outside the model, and a leak scan checks what comes back.

items.title: Untrusted content stays labelled
items.body: Web pages and other people's words, where prompt injection hides, are marked untrusted from end to end. They can inform the agent, but they can't trigger a send, a delete or a change without approval.

items.title: One workspace per customer
items.body: Each customer's agents, memory and receipts are isolated by row-level security. Test and live are separate worlds: a test key can't even see a live workspace.

items.title: A kill switch that works mid-run
items.body: Suspend a workspace and its runs stop at the next step boundary, not at the end of the job.

definition.body: OpenLegion is a hosted agent harness for running secure AI agents in production inside SaaS products and AI apps. A developer defines the agent and its tools as code. OpenLegion runs one isolated workspace per end customer, checks every tool call against policy, keeps a receipt for each action, stops for approval at three walls, meters usage against per-customer credit caps, and keeps each model tier on current models. Integration is an HTTP API and signed webhooks, with a TypeScript kit in development.

items.a: A platform for SaaS companies to put AI agents inside their own product. You define the agent and its tools as code; OpenLegion runs one workspace per customer, with policy checks, approvals, receipts and per-customer caps.

items.q: What's the easiest way to add AI agents to my app?
items.a: Use a hosted agent harness instead of building one. With OpenLegion you define the agent and its tools as code, create a workspace for each customer with one API call, and put the chat in your own UI. Tool calling, approvals, spending caps, isolation and receipts are already handled.

items.q: How long does an integration take?
items.a: The kit's target is ten minutes to an agent calling one of your own functions in your app, in test mode. About an hour gets you your real tools and webhooks, and under a day gets you live.

items.q: Do my customers sign up with OpenLegion?
items.a: No. Your backend creates a workspace for each customer with one API call. Your users never see an OpenLegion login, email or logo.

items.q: Will OpenLegion ever contact my customers?
items.a: No. It's a hard rule in the platform: no emails, messages or notifications to your customers. Anything they should know reaches you as a webhook, and you decide what to tell them.

items.q: How do the agent's tools reach my product?
items.a: Tools are your own functions, defined with the kit, or your own MCP server. Every call is signed and names the customer it's for, so your code can check it before doing anything.

Your agent's tools are your own functions, defined with the kit, or your own MCP server, so it can work with anything your product already connects to. Web search and page fetching are built in, and results reach your backend as signed webhooks.

items.q: Where does work stop for approval?
items.a: At three walls only: reaching a third party, deleting data, and acting on untrusted content. Your customer approves in your UI and the decision is recorded as theirs.
In credits. Your org prepays one pool, and each customer's workspace draws from it under the caps you set. Partner pricing is shared with early-access partners.

items.q: Is OpenLegion affordable for a small team?
items.a: You pay only for what runs. An idle workspace uses no credits, test mode moves no money, and per-customer caps stop runaway spend before it happens. Partner pricing is shared with early-access partners.
Yes. Test and live are separate worlds inside one org, with separate keys. Test mode runs real models on a monthly test allowance, and a scripted model for deterministic CI.

A template picks a model tier rather than a model id. We keep each tier on current models, so your agents move to newer models without you tracking releases, and you choose the trade between quality and cost per agent product.

items.q: Do you have SOC 2 or ISO 27001?
items.a: Not yet, and we don't claim them. The security page lists what the platform enforces today and what we don't claim.
It's in private beta. We're onboarding a small number of partners; request early access and we'll be in touch.

production.q: How does OpenLegion keep AI agents secure in production?
production.a: Security is enforced by the platform, outside the model. Each customer's agents, memory and receipts are isolated in their own workspace. Every tool call is checked against policy before it runs, keys stay in a vault the model never sees, and untrusted content can't trigger a send, a delete or a change without approval. Every step leaves a receipt. The security page lists what we enforce and what we don't claim.

platformSchema.orgDescription: OpenLegion is the AI agent platform for SaaS companies and AI app builders: a hosted agent harness with one workspace per end customer, policy-checked actions, approvals, receipts and per-customer caps.
platformSchema.softwareDescription: A hosted agent harness for running secure AI agents in production inside SaaS products and AI apps. Developers define agents and tools as code; OpenLegion runs one isolated workspace per end customer, checks every tool call against policy, keeps receipts, stops for approval at three walls, meters usage against per-customer caps, and keeps model tiers on current models.

billingPage.title: Pricing, and how billing works
billingPage.lede: We're setting partner prices with our first partners, and we'll share them with you when you get access. What's already settled is how money moves, and that's all below.

items.title: One prepaid pool for your org
items.body: You fund one pool of credits. Every customer's workspace draws from it, so you manage one balance, not hundreds. We warn you before it runs low.

items.title: A cap per customer that mirrors your plans
items.body: Give each workspace a monthly and a daily cap, hard or soft, renewing on the day your customer's plan renews. New workspaces take your template's default cap.

items.title: A reached cap is a refusal, not a bill
items.body: The run is refused before it starts, and a webhook fires so you can show your own upgrade screen. Usage alerts arrive at 50, 80 and 100 percent.

items.title: Top-ups are credit grants
items.body: Sell a customer extra usage and grant it to their workspace. Grants are spent after the monthly allowance, oldest expiry first, and what's left returns to your pool.

items.title: Usage you can show your customers
items.body: Each workspace reports credits used, reserved and remaining straight from the ledger, so the "credits left" in your UI is always right.

items.title: Test mode moves no money
items.body: Test workspaces run real models on a monthly test allowance, and a scripted model at no cost for deterministic CI.

items.title: Archiving returns the float
items.body: Archive a workspace when a customer leaves and its unused credits go back to your pool. An idle workspace uses no credits at all.

billingPage.ctaBody: Tell us how you price your own plans and we'll show you how caps and grants map onto them.
billingPage.direct: Looking for the OpenLegion app for your own team? It's behind a waitlist while we focus on partners.

faq.a: Not yet. We're setting them with our first partners, and every early-access partner gets them before going live.
Model calls and tool runs, metered in whole credits against the workspace that ran them. Every action's receipt shows its cost.

faq.q: Can a customer go over their cap?
faq.a: Only if you make the cap soft, with an overage percentage you choose. A hard cap refuses the run before it starts.

faq.q: What happens if our pool runs out?
faq.a: You're warned while it's low. Once it's empty, new runs are refused rather than run on credit.

trustPage.title: What we can promise, and what we can't
trustPage.lede: OpenLegion runs agents inside your product, on behalf of your customers. Below is what the platform enforces, written plainly enough to hold us to, and then what we don't claim.

now.title: Every action passes policy first
now.body: Each tool call is an intent checked by one policy engine before it runs, and every action leaves a receipt.

now.title: Approval at three walls
now.body: Reaching a third party on someone's behalf, deleting data, and acting on untrusted content. Decisions are made by a person, never by an agent and never by us.

now.title: A vault the model never sees
now.body: Secrets are encrypted at rest, brokered and injected outside the model, which only holds a handle. A leak scan checks tool output on the way back.

now.title: Untrusted content is labelled
now.body: Content from the web, files and other people is labelled untrusted end to end, and cannot trigger a send, a delete or a change on its own.

now.title: Isolation by row-level security
now.body: Each workspace's data is isolated in the database itself, and cross-tenant tests run against it.

now.title: Spend stops before it happens
now.body: Credits are reserved before a step runs. When a cap or balance is reached, the work is refused, not run and billed later.

now.title: A kill switch at the step boundary
now.body: Suspending a workspace stops its running work at the next step, not at the end of the job.

trustPage.apiTitle: Part of the v1 partner API (private beta)

api.title: One workspace per customer
api.body: Each of your customers gets their own workspace, created and found by your own reference.

api.title: Test and live never meet
api.body: Separate keys and separate worlds. A key from one mode gets a 404 for the other's objects, so nothing leaks across.

api.title: Keys you can scope and rotate
api.body: Org keys are hashed at rest, scoped, rotatable with an overlap window, and revocable. Live keys are shown once.

api.title: Signed calls to your tools
api.body: Every call to your tools is signed and names the customer it's for, so your code can verify it before acting.

api.title: Signed webhooks
api.body: Events are signed with a timestamped HMAC and delivered at least once, with a stable event id.

trustPage.customers: OpenLegion never contacts a partner's customers. No emails, messages, notifications or OpenLegion branding reach them; everything leaves through your webhooks and API. You can export, archive or erase a customer's workspace by API.
trustPage.notClaimed: We hold no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA certification, and we don't describe the platform as "GDPR compliant" or "EU AI Act compliant": compliance is a property of how a system is used, not a badge a vendor awards itself. No system that reads the open web is immune to prompt injection, and we publish no attack-success percentages, because a number without a published method is marketing. Web search and page fetches run on our servers, not inside the code sandbox, so "fully sandboxed" would be wrong. We have not commissioned a third-party penetration test. When any of that changes, this page changes with it.
trustPage.contact: Found something we should know about? Email {email} and we'll answer.
trustPage.ctaBody: We'll walk them through the harness, the API contract and this page, line by line.
